text:
alex chen: Heads up — kicking off a 4-week "boundary thinning" sprint to pull routing-core (hotpath) out of the orchestration process. RFC follow-up: we need an ownership handoff, migration plan, and SLO guardrails. Goal is smaller blast radius + faster iteration on routing rules.

maria gonzalez: Why now? Any perf regressions or is this mostly tech-debt cleanup?

alex chen: A bit of both. Latency tail increases when orchestration spikes; also several teams want to iterate on routing without touching orchestrator.

jamal roberts: Concern: both services touch the tenant routing table in the primary DB. How are we avoiding cross-service races during cutover? :thinking:

sasha li: +1. We should prefer a migration that avoids dual-writes for long. My two cents: shadow traffic + read-replica for verification, then a short write-shard window.

alex chen: Proposed phased approach: shadow traffic -> canary tenants -> write-shard (short window) -> promote. Fallback policy to route back to orchestrator if errors > 1% or latency > 50ms over baseline.

maria gonzalez: What about event ordering? Orchestrator currently injects enrichment events synchronously. If we split, we risk reordering.

jamal roberts: We should add a sequencing token on the routing events. That lets new service validate monotonicity without global locks. Minimal proto change.

sasha li: Agree. Contract tests need to include sequencing token semantics. Also add idempotency keys for retries.

alex chen: Draft rollout steps (working):
```
1) deploy routing-core service in parallel (read-only)
2) mirror (shadow) 100% of hotpath requests to routing-core for 48h
3) run compare jobs (latency, output-diff) + contract tests
4) enable canary group (5% tenants) -> allow writes to new service for those tenants
5) run write-shard migration for remaining tenants during low traffic window (30-45m)
6) promote and decommission orchestrator's routing hotpath
```

jamal roberts: Shadowing + compare jobs sound good. Who owns the compare pipeline? I can take that but we need metrics defined.

maria gonzalez: I can own perf benchmarks and the SLO guardrails. Suggest SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency no worse than current + 10% during canary, errors < 0.5% for canary.

sasha li: I'll add contract tests and update our e2e suite. We should add an integration test that replays a day's worth of events to assert no state drift.

alex chen: Owner picks: jamal for compare pipeline, maria for SLO/perf signoff, sasha for contract/e2e. I'll draft the runbook and the rollback playbook.

maria gonzalez: Cost note — routing-core will add GPUs? No, just smaller CPU pool for now. But shadowing doubles hotpath requests which could spike infra costs during validation window. Budget owners should be warned. :money_with_wings:

jamal roberts: For DB migration: propose temporary read-replica and short write lock during shard switch. We minimize dual-writes to the canary group. We need DB team signoff.

sasha li: Add tracing hooks (trace-id passthrough) so we can correlate path through orchestrator vs routing-core during shadowing. Without that debugging will be painful.

alex chen: Good call. Observability checklist: traces, per-tenant request counters, diff metric (outputs-mismatched), latency histograms, rollout heartbeat. Maria pls define thresholds.

maria gonzalez: Will do. Suggest adding automated alert: if diffs > 0.1% over 1h -> auto rollback.

jamal roberts: Testing concerns: some downstream services rely on a side-effect from orchestrator order. Might need a short compatibility shim for a few days. Plan for that in runbook.

sasha li: I'll prepare compatibility shims and feature flags. Use toggles with default-off so we can enable per-tenant quickly.

alex chen: Timeline proposal: Week 0 (spec + infra tickets), Week 1 (implement shadow & compare), Week 2 (canary), Week 3 (shard migration + promote), Week 4 (cleanup). Flexible if DB signoff takes longer.

maria gonzalez: Can we reserve a rollback maintenance window with SRE on call for shard migration? We'll want fast hands.

alex chen: Yes — request will go into the SRE calendar. Also will book an hour after canary to review metrics before promotion.

jamal roberts: Who's writing the ticket list? I can open CORE-1234 with sub-tasks, then we can triage.

alex chen: Perfect. Assign owners in the ticket. Also include a rollback playbook section with exact commands to flip tenants back. Keep it < 5 commands.

sasha li: I'll add contract test matrix to the ticket. Also schedule a short spike to prototype sequencing token in a branch.

alex chen: Meeting to align: tomorrow 10am PT, 30m. Agenda: DB migration plan, observability checklist, canary tenant selection, cost estimate. Please bring blockers.

maria gonzalez: 👍 I'll prepare perf baseline numbers.

jamal roberts: 👍 I'll bring compare pipeline sketch.

sasha li: 👍 I'll bring e2e matrix.

alex chen: Thanks team. If anyone sees a non-obvious dependency (eg. third-party integrations), flag it here before the meeting. :eyes:

 taylor-bot: New ticket CORE-1234 created: boundary-thinning-runbook (owners: alex, jamal, maria, sasha).

alex chen: Awesome — moving to inbox. :shipit:

maria gonzalez: Small note: we should capture postmortem triggers in the runbook (data-loss, >5% customer impact).

alex chen: Agreed. Adding that now.

jamal roberts: One more ops nit: prepare a read-only debug endpoint that returns the last processed sequence for a tenant. Makes migration debugging much faster.

sasha li: Will add.

alex chen: End of thread — thanks all, see you at 10am.
